title: How to Switch from Consensus to Storylane
summary: Storylane vs Consensus for presales: video-led demo automation vs interactive and sandbox demos, plus pricing, analytics, security and how to switch.
body_markdown:
If you run presales or sales engineering and you are weighing Storylane against Consensus, the short answer is this. Consensus grew up as video-led demo automation for enterprise deals: recorded, branching video demos sent to a buying committee, with deep stakeholder tracking on who watched what. Storylane grew up as interactive demos you capture from your own product (screenshot, video or full HTML), plus sandbox demos for live calls and Hubs for deal rooms. Both now sell much broader platforms, so the real question is which starting point matches how your team demos today.


This page comes from Storylane, so read it with that in mind. We have tried to be specific about where Consensus is strongest, and every Consensus detail below was checked on its own website on October 23, 2026.


## Who is Consensus today?


Consensus is still an independent company operating under its own name (the site footer reads Consensus Sales, LLC). Its[About page](https://goconsensus.com/about) dates the first demo automation prototype to 2013 and the company launch to 2015. It has grown largely by acquisition:


- **ReachSuite (September 2024):** added live product simulations and interactive tours to the video platform ([press release](https://goconsensus.com/press-release/consensus-acquires-reachsuite) ).
- **Peel (agreement announced April 2026, closed by June 2026):** conversational AI agents that turn content into two-way buyer conversations ([press release](https://goconsensus.com/press-release/consensus-to-acquire-peel) ).
- **Saleo (June 2026):** injects tailored demo data into your real product for live demos ([press release](https://goconsensus.com/press-release/consensus-to-acquire-saleo) ).


Consensus now describes itself as an agentic product experience platform covering AI demo agents, interactive tours, video and live demos. If you last looked at it as a video tool, look again: the scope is wider. The practical consequence for an evaluator is that several of these capabilities arrived through acquisitions in the last two years, so ask in the demo which pieces sit in one product and which are still separate apps or logins.


## What each platform is built for


### Consensus: video-led demo automation, now with tours, agents and live data


The core of Consensus is still the[on-demand video demo](https://goconsensus.com/on-demand-video-demos) . You record or upload clips, arrange them in the Demo Creator, and add branching questions so each buyer picks the parts relevant to their role. Demos are delivered through DemoBoards (a branded landing page per buyer), and champions can forward them to colleagues. Consensus also sells[interactive product tours](https://goconsensus.com/interactive-product-tours) (HTML capture, video capture and sandbox tours),[AI agents](https://goconsensus.com/ai-agents) for lead qualification and autonomous demos, and[live demos powered by Saleo](https://goconsensus.com/live-demo-software) that put generated demo data inside your native product.


### Storylane: interactive, HTML and sandbox demos your team builds itself


Storylane's Demo Suite starts with capture. You click through your product with the Chrome extension or desktop app, and Storylane records it as a screenshot, video or[HTML interactive demo](https://www.storylane.io/interactive-demos) , adding guides as you go. HTML demos can be edited without code (text, numbers, images) or by prompting the AI HTML editor, and personalization tokens swap names, logos and currencies per account. For live calls,[sandbox demos](https://www.storylane.io/sandbox-demo) give a free-roam clone of your product with presenter mode and private sales notes.[Hubs](https://www.storylane.io/buyer-hub) bundle demos, PDFs and videos into one deal room per account.


The short version: Consensus is strongest when the demo is a recorded expert walkthrough that a buying committee watches. Storylane is strongest when the buyer should click through the product themselves, or when your SEs need a stable environment for live calls.

## How buyers experience each one


A Consensus buyer typically opens a DemoBoard link. They answer a few questions about what matters to them, and Consensus assembles a playlist of video segments and tours for that role. If they forward the link, Consensus records the new viewer as a stakeholder. This works well for a large committee where many people will never attend a call but still want to see the product explained by an expert voice.


A Storylane buyer clicks through the product itself: hotspots and tooltips guide each step, chapters let them jump to the part they care about, and HTML demos behave like the real interface. For a technical evaluator who wants to poke at the product rather than watch someone else do it, that is a closer experience to a trial. Try the one below.


Neither format wins for every buyer. Video carries narrative and an expert voice; a clickable demo carries hands-on proof. We cover the trade-off in more depth in[interactive demos vs product videos](https://www.storylane.io/blog/interactive-demos-vs-product-videos) .


## Building and maintaining demos as an SE team


This is where the two approaches feel most different day to day.


- **Recording vs capturing.** A Consensus video demo is a recording. When your UI changes, the affected clips usually need to be re-recorded or re-edited. A Storylane HTML demo is a captured copy of the interface, so you can change a label, a number or a chart in the editor (or with an AI prompt) without recapturing the flow.
- **Personalization per account.** Consensus personalizes through branching questions and AI prompts that rework a tour. Storylane uses tokens for names, logos, currencies and dates, filled in from the share menu, a lead form or URL parameters, plus the AI editor for bigger changes.
- **Live calls.** If your SEs need to demo the real product with realistic data, Consensus (through Saleo) is built for that. If they would rather present a stable clone that cannot break mid-call, Storylane's sandbox demos and presenter mode are built for that.


If your SE team is also weighing AI agents that run demos on their own, our playbook on[agentic AI demos for sales engineering teams](https://www.storylane.io/blog/agentic-ai-demos-for-sales-engineering-teams) covers what to check before deploying one.


## Analytics: what each tells you about a deal


Consensus's[Demolytics](https://goconsensus.com/overview/demolytics) is organised around the buying group. It reports on six levels, from buyer group analysis down to individual demo performance, and tracks demos sent, stakeholders discovered through forwarding, view rates, which sections each person chose and documents downloaded. If you need to show leadership how demos influence multi-stakeholder deals, this is a real strength.


Storylane's analytics are organised around the demo and the account: views, time spent and completion per demo, user-level engagement through personalized and recipient links, and[Demo Signals](https://www.storylane.io/demo-signals) , which identifies companies viewing your demos, scores intent as low, medium or high, and sends Slack, email or webhook alerts. Account Reveal identifies 250, 2,500 or 10,000 visitors per month on Starter, Growth and Premium. Growth and above add A/B testing and deal intelligence tied to your CRM.


Whichever you pick, the hard part is tying demo engagement to pipeline. Our[guide to lead attribution for interactive demos](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) walks through the setup.


## Integrations


Both cover the core sales stack. Consensus lists Salesforce, HubSpot, Pardot, Marketo, Eloqua, Gong, Outreach, Slack, Gmail, Outlook, G2, SourceForge and an open REST API on its[integrations page](https://goconsensus.com/integrations) , and its pricing page says integrations are included at no extra cost.


Storylane's[integrations](https://www.storylane.io/integrations) include HubSpot, Salesforce, Marketo, Pardot, Dynamics 365, Freshsales, Gong, Outreach, Slack, Zapier, Segment, Google Analytics, Intercom, G2 and a Gmail plugin. HubSpot and Zapier are included from Starter, and the Salesforce integration and app come with Premium.


## Security and access control


Both will pass a typical security review. Consensus's[security center](https://goconsensus.com/consensus-security-center/) lists SOC 2 Type 2 attestation, encryption in transit and at rest, annual third-party penetration tests, hosting on AWS and OCI, SSO, two-factor authentication on DemoBoards and role-based access control that admins can customize.


Storylane lists SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance, SSO (SAML) from Premium, and per-demo protection: passwords, link expiry dates, domain-restricted access with an emailed code, and private demo links on Enterprise ([docs](https://docs.storylane.io/sharing-demos/demo-protection-and-security) ). Its roles are Admin, Creator, Presenter and a free Viewer seat ([docs](https://docs.storylane.io/account/managing-team) ).


## Pricing


**Consensus is quote-based.** Its[pricing page](https://goconsensus.com/pricing) no longer lists plan prices. It says pricing is built from per-user licenses plus optional usage-based capabilities, with integrations free, and asks you to fill out a form. We found no free plan or self-serve trial on the site. Earlier versions of this article quoted list prices; we removed them because Consensus no longer publishes them.


**Storylane publishes its prices** on its[plans page](https://www.storylane.io/plans) . Billed yearly, Demo Suite costs:


- **Free:** $0, one seat, one published demo.
- **Starter:** $40 per month for one seat, plus $40 per additional seat ($50 billed monthly).
- **Growth:** $500 per month with five seats ($625 billed monthly). Adds HTML demos, personalization tokens and A/B testing.
- **Premium:** $1,200 per month with ten seats ($1,500 billed monthly). Adds Hubs, Salesforce, SSO and presenter demos.
- **Enterprise:** custom pricing. Adds sandbox demos, API access and private demo links.


For an SE team, the plan that matters is usually Premium or Enterprise, because that is where Salesforce, SSO and sandbox demos sit. Compare your Consensus quote against those tiers rather than against Starter. For building the business case either way, see[demo automation ROI for presales and SE leaders](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-automation-roi-presales-se-leaders) .


## Choose Consensus if


- Your buyers respond best to recorded expert walkthroughs, and you want branching video paths for each role on a large buying committee.
- You want live demos in your real product with generated data, rather than a captured clone.
- Stakeholder discovery (seeing who a champion forwarded the demo to) is the metric your leadership cares about most.
- You need custom roles and permissions across a large, multi-team organisation.
- You are buying an enterprise platform through a sales-led process anyway and want video, tours, agents and live demos from one vendor.


## Choose Storylane if


- You want buyers to click through the product themselves, with HTML demos that look and behave like the real interface.
- Your UI changes often and you would rather edit captured screens than re-record videos.
- Your SEs want a stable sandbox and presenter mode for live calls, and reps should be able to send personalized demos without an SE building each one.
- You want to start on a free plan or a trial and see published prices before talking to sales.
- You need exports (GIF, video, PDF, Word) for email, enablement docs and offline use.


If neither fits cleanly, our roundup of[Consensus alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/consensus-alternatives) compares other options, and the wider[demo automation tools comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/best-demo-automation-tools-2026-real-tradeoffs-for-each-vendor) covers the trade-offs for each vendor.


## Switching from Consensus to Storylane


Most of your Consensus demo content carries over into Storylane. A practical sequence:


1. **Check your Consensus renewal date** and work back from it, so you can run both tools in parallel for a few weeks instead of cutting over on the last day.
2. **Inventory what is actually in use.** List the videos and DemoBoards tied to active deals, the ones reps send most, and the ones embedded in sequences or on your website. Those are your first rebuilds. Ask Consensus which source files and engagement data you can export before the contract ends.
3. **Decide format per demo.** Flows where the buyer should explore become HTML interactive demos, captured from your live product with the Storylane extension. Narrated explainers you want to keep can go through Media to Demo, which turns an existing product video into an interactive demo.
4. **Rebuild DemoBoards as Hubs.** Group demos, PDFs and videos per persona or deal, and add interest screens so buyers rank what matters to them before they open anything.
5. **Reconnect your stack.** Set up lead forms, connect your CRM (Salesforce comes with Premium), and configure Slack or email alerts so reps see engagement.
6. **Replace every old link.** Swap Consensus links in email sequences, CRM templates, website embeds and sales decks for Storylane share links or embeds, then retire the old ones.


On Growth, Premium and Enterprise, Storylane's demo specialist team provides onboarding and training, which helps when you are rebuilding a library rather than starting from scratch.


Want to see how your current Consensus demos would look as interactive or sandbox demos?[Book a demo with Storylane](https://www.storylane.io/request-demo) and bring one of your most-sent videos.
